page: Amazon Web Services c7i.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of memory per core. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance demonstrates average single-core capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1938.18 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1665.0. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression (28.29 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (10.92 GB/sec) perform at average levels. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core performance is rated as poor at 1991.39, and the Geekbench multi-core score is weak at 2034.0. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds of 11.05 GB/sec and 11.76 GB/sec respectively, both falling into the poor category.

Given its hardware profile, the c7i.large offers an entry-point into the Intel-based compute-optimized family. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require dedicated CPU cycles but have low memory footprints. However, the low memory capacity of 4.0 GB and poor memory bandwidth present clear tradeoffs, making it unsuitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data processing. It is best suited for lightweight compute tasks, single-threaded applications, basic web serving, and small-scale text processing.
